blocks.content: A simple paddle bounce just flips ballSpeedY. That works, but makes every bounce identical regardless of where the ball lands. Instead, map the hit position on the paddle to a bounce angle. Center hit → straight up (0°). Left edge → 60° left. Right edge → 60° right.

-Math.abs(...) on speedY ensures the ball always exits upward, even if floating point drift makes cos(angle) slightly negative. Math.hypot preserves the total speed magnitude when recalculating direction.

Math.hypot calculates the magnitude of the velocity vector using √(x² + y²). When we change the ball's direction using trigonometry, we use this magnitude to ensure the total speed remains constant, preventing gradual speed drift caused by floating point errors.
